title: Garment stitching: which outline chains of the placed pieces are sewn together (stitcher)

chain.description: named points on the outline, in sewing order; the outline is walked between the first and the last the way that passes every listed point (an exact list of one way wins; otherwise ambiguous is an error)

piece.description: a placed piece of the assembly (derived names included)

reverse.description: sew this chain from its last point to its first

trim_start_m.description: cut this much off the start of the chain as listed (a seam that ends between named points)

trim_end_m.description: cut this much off the end of the chain as listed

line.description: a straight polyline through named points inside the piece (a dart leg down to its apex); trims do not apply

parts.description: chains sewn one after the other (an armhole of front, yoke and back)

reverse.description: reverse the whole side (part order and every part)

onto.description: attach: the host piece; side b is the closest point of its placed surface to every sample of side a

assembly.description: path of the assembly JSON (repository-relative) or sha256:<hex> of one in assert/assemblies

max_length_diff_pct.description: tolerance of ease none when a seam has no tolerance_pct

max_gap_m.description: largest world gap of a seam without allow_far

kind.description: plain: a flat join, the pieces end on opposite sides of the seam; ease / gather: plain with a length difference; fold: the pieces end on the same side (a facing turned in, a bag sewn round its edge, a placket folded over the slit); join_mirror: a piece and its mirror_of/clone_of twin along the centre edge; dart: two legs of one piece; attach: side a sewn onto the surface of the host piece named by b {onto} (patch pockets, flaps)

mode.description: none: lengths equal within tolerance_pct; distribute: up to 5 % spread along the seam; gather: up to the declared ratio

ratio.description: gather: the largest allowed long/short length ratio (recorded for the simulation)

allow_far.description: the world gap may exceed defaults.max_gap_m (the simulation closes it)

allow_crossings.description: why sewing segments of the initial layout cross although the seam is oriented right (pieces placed apart or rotated, a jog in the outline, a step between layers): crossings are then reported, not judged; the sewing rule is always judged

edge.description: an edge id FROM-TO of the alignment result
